llm.summary: The skill's high-level purpose (a runtime security plugin) is plausible, but the instructions claim both local-only sanitization and remote/Core-based detection, rely on installing external plugin code that is not included for review, and auto-registers/saves API keys—these contradictions and the centralization of agent credentials warrant caution.

dimensions.detail: The name/description (a runtime security plugin) match the actions described (install a plugin via openclaw, provide status/config commands). However the SKILL.md simultaneously claims 'Local sanitization' and that 'All security detection is performed by Core' (remote). That is an internal contradiction: a security product that does detection remotely but guarantees sensitive data 'never leaves your machine' is not coherent without a clear explanation of what is sent to Core and how it's sanitized.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The instructions tell the agent to run 'openclaw plugins install @openguardrails/moltguard' and other plugin commands, and to read a sample file under ~/.openclaw/extensions/... (which is reasonable). They also instruct/describe an automatic auto-registration flow with Core and storing credentials under ~/.openclaw/credentials/moltguard/. The SKILL.md is vague about what data is sent to Core, when sanitization happens, and what the /og_* commands actually do — granting the plugin and service broad discretion to access local files and agent state.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec or code is bundled with this skill; the SKILL.md instructs use of the openclaw plugin manager to fetch and install @openguardrails/moltguard. That is expected for a plugin, but it means executable code will be downloaded and run from the registry (not included in this package for review). The lack of bundled code prevents static review and increases risk relative to instruction-only tips.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill itself requests no environment variables, but its onboarding claims automatic registration with a remote 'Core', storing credentials at ~/.openclaw/credentials/moltguard/, and a flow to share Agent ID/API Key to claim agents. Centralizing agent API keys and having the plugin auto-create/save credentials is plausible for a SaaS security product, but it is a sensitive capability and should be explicitly justified and transparent. The SKILL.md does not declare what is transmitted to Core, nor whether full file contents or only signatures/sanitized artifacts are sent.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request 'always: true' and does not declare elevated platform privileges, but its described onboarding will create local credentials and persistent configuration under ~/.openclaw, and link agents to a central account (shared quota). That persistence is normal for a plugin, but it increases blast radius if the remote service or plugin is malicious or misconfigured.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This package is a wrapper/instructions to install a third‑party plugin (not the plugin code itself). Before installing: (1) Review the actual plugin code that 'openclaw plugins install' will fetch (check the GitHub repo and release source and verify the package owner), (2) confirm you trust the Core service—installing will auto-register agents and store API keys at ~/.openclaw/credentials/moltguard/, which effectively grants the remote service access to agent activity and potentially uploaded artifacts, (3) ask the vendor/documentation exactly what is sent to Core vs sanitized locally (the SKILL.md contradicts itself), (4) consider installing in an isolated/test agent first and monitor outbound network traffic, and (5) avoid claiming/centralizing production agents until you validate privacy, retention, and access policies and rotate any created keys. If you want, provide the plugin package name/registry link or the repository tarball and I can re-evaluate with the actual code.
